inputs_used: content-system/seo/link-map.csv (grep: no Paros or Antiparos pages)

payload.title: Paros Wedding Venues and How to Get Married There
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, planning 40 to 150 guests who will fly in via a European hub or Athens. They want a Cycladic island that feels calmer than Mykonos or Santorini, have Paros on the shortlist, and now need to choose an area (Naoussa and the north, Parikia and the west, the inland villages, or the east and south coast), compare venues on the same terms, and understand how a legal or symbolic ceremony works on the island before they commit.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation so an advisor can check availability, ceremony options and house rules for the couple's shortlisted Paros venues on their dates and guest count.
payload.angle: One guide that answers both halves of the search: where to marry on Paros and how to get married there. Every venue listed says on its own official site that it hosts weddings and is described with the same fields in the same order (setting, ceremony options as stated, capacity, rooms, exclusive use, one standout), grouped by area so a couple can see how a Naoussa hotel, a Parikia or inland estate and an east or south coast resort differ. House rules a venue does not publish are written as 'Not published' and gathered on a booking checklist. The legal section is a main section built only from official sources: civil, Greek Orthodox and symbolic ceremonies as official sources describe them, the Municipality of Paros civil ceremony only as its official page states, and the Australian steps through the Embassy in Athens and Smartraveller, dated as at November 2026. No venue count in the title and no padding: list however many qualify (aim 8 to 10).
must_include: Intro with a direct answer in the first 100 words: Paros's main wedding areas, that the right one depends on guest count, ceremony type and setting, and that the guide also covers how to marry there; link /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues prominently and the hub /destinations/europe/greece.
At a glance: 5-column table (venue, area, type, ceremony options, capacity) with 'Not published' where not published.

How to compare like for like: hotel or resort vs estate or winery vs villa with exclusive use vs event venue; ceremony type on site only as stated; seated capacity; rooms; the single Wedded Advisor line and Wedded Concierge invitation sit in this section.

Choosing an area: Naoussa and the north; Parikia and the west; inland villages (Lefkes, Marpissa); east and south coast (Golden Beach, Drios); Antiparos as a short nearby note only if venues there qualify. Practical guidance from visitgreece.gr or venue sources only; no unsourced distances or drive times.

Venues by area, from official pages only, each with the same fields in the same order: location and setting; ceremony options as stated; capacity; rooms; exclusive use where published, else 'Not published'; one standout detail. Venues are discovered and verified by the fact batches (A Naoussa and north; B Parikia, west and inland; C east and south coast plus Antiparos), each by a live read of its own official site; no candidate names are fixed at this stage. Booking checklist for house rules not published. No prices.

How to get married there (main section, official sources only): civil, Greek Orthodox and symbolic ceremonies as official sources state them; civil ceremony at the Municipality of Paros (Dimos Parou) with steps, documents and lead times only if an official municipal page is read live, else 'check with the municipality and the embassy, including any fees'; Australian steps (certificate of no impediment and notarial services at the Australian Embassy Athens; Smartraveller getting married overseas and recognition in Australia), dated 'as at November 2026' once; link the Greece venues guide's legal section. Nothing implies the Advisor handles legal, church or religious paperwork.
Getting there: Paros airport and ferries from official sources only; no transfer arrangements.
When to marry: hnms.gr data only if for Paros or a clearly labelled nearby station, else Smartraveller heat and wildfire advice.

FAQ (5 to 6): Which part of Paros suits a wedding? Can we book a venue or villa on Paros for exclusive use? Can Australians legally marry on Paros? Can we have a civil ceremony at the Paros town hall? How do guests get to Paros? When is the best time to marry on Paros?

Links: /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues (prominent), /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages, /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding-venues, /destinations/europe/greece, /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions (once), /wonderland-concierge (primary in comparison section and at close), /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=paros-wedding-venues&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing.
Close: shortlist with a Wedded Advisor.
avoid: Any price, fee, minimum spend or amount; any capacity, room count, distance or time not on an official source.
Venues without a weddings offer on their own official site (live read, never snippets alone); anything off Paros except a short Antiparos note.

Research talk in copy (what we could or could not find, trace or confirm; sources; method; what the internet says; 'you will often read'; myths sections); per-line source credits; hedge stacking; 'often told' more than once and never 'it is often told that'; customs with meanings or origins stated as fact.
Ranking as 'best'; a venue count in the title or headings; padding to reach a number.
Competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs, booking and review sites, Instagram, Pinterest or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording or images.
Vendor names other than venues; venue contact or business details; transfer arrangements; implying partnerships or preferred rates.

Wedded Privileges; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; more than one Advisor line in the body; 'from first idea to the last dance', 'last dance'; anything implying the Advisor handles legal, church or religious paperwork.
Clichés (fairytale, dream day, breathtaking), exclamation marks, pasted or bracketed keywords in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding.

payload.inclusion_rule: Venue's own official site says it hosts weddings (live read, never search snippets alone). Mix of boutique and luxury hotels, estates and wineries, villas and event venues. 'Cycladic' framing only where the venue's own description uses it.
